evals.prompt: Create specs for a self-hosted enterprise runtime with adapters, queues, policy, observability, and sandboxed tools.
evals.expected_output: Creates foundation, domains, capabilities, contracts, tech specs, NFRs, and definition-readiness coverage.

evals.prompt: Review these specs for enterprise gaps and unhappy paths.
evals.expected_output: Finds missing timeout, retry, DLQ/manual intervention, cleanup, adapter health, test, and definition-readiness gaps.

evals.prompt: Improve the specs so implementation planning can be fully autonomous.
evals.expected_output: Adds missing contracts, interfaces, data model, failure handling, test strategy, planning simulation evidence, and readiness gates instead of putting spec closure into the plan.

evals.prompt: Approve specs where the simulated implementation ticket would still need to decide API shape, error behavior, and test coverage.
evals.expected_output: Refuses approval, reports the missing decisions as spec gaps, and requires enough detail to produce a decision ledger, contract traceability, and acceptance test matrix.

evals.prompt: Review specs for a backend service wave where the web client is planned later.
evals.expected_output: Allows service-wave readiness only if the service API, auth, schemas, errors, lifecycle, compatibility, tests, and future client-facing contracts are complete; otherwise blocks with spec gaps.

evals.prompt: Make these specs implementation-ready for parallel AI agents without drift.
evals.expected_output: Adds no-drift, ambiguity, interface, end-to-end, contradiction, wave-readiness, ownership, write-scope, contract-traceability, acceptance-matrix, and verification evidence instead of asking implementers to decide behavior.

evals.prompt: Review specs for a Go GraphQL service consumed by a TypeScript frontend.
evals.expected_output: Requires explicit end-to-end semantic mapping for GraphQL nullability, omitted variables, TypeScript optional or undefined fields, Go pointer/value/null handling, generated types, resolver errors, and cross-layer fixtures.

evals.prompt: Update approved specs that materially change an already implemented async Python worker flow.
evals.expected_output: Requires async runtime semantics plus a separate plans/migrations migration plan covering impact, rollout, compatibility, rollback, verification, and ownership.

evals.prompt: Approve specs with weak assumptions and no self-audit evidence.
evals.expected_output: Refuses approval until self_audit_gate passes with honest uncertainty, weakest assumptions, evidence, and remaining blockers.
